subject: Post-call: RAG eval & retrieval configuration recommendations for Acerosys
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khanna <samir@acerosys.com>, Marta López <marta.lopez@acerosys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: RAG eval & retrieval configuration recommendations for Acerosys

Hi Samir / Marta —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we discussed so the team has it in writing. I copied Marissa from commercial for visibility.

Summary of use case
- Customer-facing knowledge base (product + policy) where answers must be grounded to internal docs (PDFs and escaped support tickets).
- Typical query distribution: short how-tos (~40%), troubleshooting (30%), and policy clarifications (30%).
- Latency SLO target: 400ms p50 for short answers, up to 1.2s p95 acceptable for long-form explanations.

High-level model fit recommendation (initial shortlist)
- Retrieval encoder: we recommend a dense encoder (SBERT-based) hosted with FAISS for this dataset size; dimensionality 768 fits current docs.
- Candidate generator: Redwood-7B-instruct-qa (quantized) for generation baseline — best tradeoff for throughput and quality in our internal benchmarks for similar KB sizes.
- Reranker: a cross-encoder (T5-large re-ranker or MPNet cross-encoder if you need faster rerank) to re-score top-K (K=50 -> rerank top 5). Cross-encoder trend: better grounding precision, but costs more compute per-query.
- Grounding metric: use R-Precision on labeled QA pairs plus a grounded-accuracy metric (percentage of model sentences that cite a matching document id).

Initial retrieval settings to try (recommended A/B)
- Config A (precision-oriented): FAISS HNSW, k = 50, passage chunking 250 tokens, overlap 50 tokens, BM25 warm-start then switch to dense for production.
- Config B (latency-oriented): FAISS IVF PQ, k = 20, chunking 400 tokens (bigger passages to reduce reranker load), use MPNet encoder.

Evaluation plan (short pilot)
- We’ll run a 1k-query synthetic evaluation (we provided a starter prompt set attached) against both retrieval configs and two rerankers. Metrics: Exact match, R-Precision@5, grounded-accuracy, hallucination score (human-labeled subset).
- Estimated runtime: ~36 hours on a single dedicated GPU node for the full pilot when run against your sample KB.

Deliverables we’ll share after the pilot
- Per-config benchmark report (latency, token cost, precision metrics)
- Recommendation: production config + cost estimates and canary rollout plan
- Prompt set and eval harness (we’ll share the Drive folder and HubSpot link below)

Attachments: acerosys-rag-eval-instructions.pdf (pilot steps), acerosys-prompt-sets-v1.jsonl (starter prompts), acerosys-kb-sample.tar.gz (the sample docs we pulled during discovery)

Next steps (what I’ll do)
1) Kick off the pilot once you confirm sample dataset availability and sign the pilot SOW (I attached the instructions for onboarding).
2) Share an invite to a short 30-min kick-off with engineering to get access to the sample S3 bucket / Drive.
3) Marissa will follow up on commercial timeline and draft of the pilot SOW and cost estimate.

Can you confirm:
- Which environment should we use for the pilot (your S3 or a secure upload to our private tenant)?
- Any non-standard compliance constraints (data residency, redaction requirements)?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Khanna <samir@acerosys.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T16:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: RAG eval & retrieval configuration recommendations for Acerosys

Alex — thanks for the write-up, that looks thorough. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Pilot environment: we prefer to keep the sample docs in our AWS S3 (us-west-2). We can create a short-lived role and credentials for the pilot.
2) Compliance: we need all logs retained for 90 days and cannot export PII. We also require that the reranker model not be allowed to cache raw customer queries. Is that a problem?
3) SLA/pricing: Marissa — could you share a ballpark for the pilot cost + what a monthly committed plan looks like for the Dedicated option?

Two asks:
- Can you run a short AB where the reranker is T5-large and the alternative is an MPNet cross-encoder? We want to understand the precision/cost tradeoff.
- We have a small labeled set (~150 QA pairs) from past tickets; can you include that in the evaluation so we don’t start blind?

If that all sounds feasible we can get the S3 creds to you by EOD Friday and have legal sign the pilot SOW next week.

—Samir
Head of Search & Insights, Acerosys
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khanna <samir@acerosys.com>, Marta López <marta.lopez@acerosys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: RAG eval & retrieval configuration recommendations for Acerosys

Samir — appreciate the quick notes. All feasible. Short answers: 

- S3: perfect — send a short-lived role and we’ll pull the sample set into an isolated pilot bucket in our private tenant (we won’t persist any raw queries beyond the 90-day retention you requested).
- Logging/PII: we’ll enable query redaction and disable query caching on the reranker for the pilot. I’ll document the settings in the pilot runbook.
- Reranker AB: we’ll test T5-large vs MPNet cross-encoder (same train/eval split including your 150 labeled QA pairs).

Pilot timeline & next steps
1) You share S3 role + sample KB link by EOD Friday (Nov 20).
2) We schedule a 30-min engineering handoff (I’ll include our infra lead and the pilot runner).
3) Pilot run (1k queries + labeled subset) and initial results by end of next week (est. Nov 26).

Deliverables we’ll produce in the drive folder: an evaluation dashboard, raw logs (redacted per your policy), and a recommended production config with cost estimates.

I’ve attached a small runbook and a short shell script that automates the dataset import (attached in the Drive link below). For legal / procurement, Marissa will send the pilot SOW and a ballpark estimate.

Let me know if you want the reranker to return the top-1 supporting document id inline (helps traceability). That does add a small latency cost but we can include it in Config A.

Alex
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
